disclaimer: Drafting aid, not engineering. Typical/approximate values — verify with the local authority having jurisdiction. Canadian entries (CA-*) describe National Building Code of Canada adoption, not IRC adoption; ircBase is null for all of them.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.residentialCode: 2015 Alabama Residential Code (2015 IRC with AL amendments), effective 2016-10-01
AL.amendmentFlavor: Lightly amended 2015 IRC set as state minimum by the Energy & Residential Codes Board; enforcement is local and many rural counties do not inspect
specialRegimes: Coastal counties (Mobile, Baldwin) enforce high-wind provisions incl. ICC 600-2020 and FORTIFIED incentives
Alabama residential energy code (Energy & Residential Codes Board)
AL.note: UpCodes shows the 2015 IRC-based code still current in 2026; board updates have lagged. Verify locally — larger cities may amend or run ahead of the state minimum.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.residentialCode: No general statewide residential code; 2018 IRC with Alaska-specific amendments (eff. 2019-01-01) applies to AHFC-financed housing; cities adopt their own
AK.amendmentFlavor: State IRC amendments are mostly energy/ventilation (BEES); Anchorage and other deferred jurisdictions administer their own amended codes
specialRegimes: AHFC Building Energy Efficiency Standard (BEES) for state-financed homes
Municipality of Anchorage amended IRC
Severe frost depth (42-60+ in) and high seismic in south-central AK
AK.note: Large unincorporated areas have no permit/inspection regime for 1-2 family dwellings.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.residentialCode: No statewide residential code; municipalities/counties adopt the IRC individually (Phoenix and Tucson on 2018 IRC)
AZ.amendmentFlavor: Editions in use range roughly 2012-2024 by jurisdiction; only the fire code (2024 IFC) is adopted statewide
specialRegimes: Statewide International Fire Code 2024 with amendments
Sonoran Desert jurisdictions commonly amend for thermal mass/masonry construction
AZ.note: ircBase 2018 is representative of the largest cities; unincorporated county areas may have minimal or no residential enforcement.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.residentialCode: Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, Vol. III — Residential, 2021 edition (2021 IRC base), effective 2023-01-01
AR.amendmentFlavor: Moderately amended 2021 IRC issued by the State Fire Marshal as the AFPC Vol. III; local enforcement capacity varies widely
specialRegimes: Arkansas Energy Code for New Building Construction

CA.name: California
CA.residentialCode: 2025 California Residential Code (CRC), Title 24 Part 2.5 (2024 IRC base), effective 2026-01-01
CA.amendmentFlavor: Heavily amended: seismic bracing/engineering triggers, WUI Chapter 7A materials, mandatory sprinklers, Title 24 Part 6 energy; local jurisdictions may only add more-restrictive amendments
specialRegimes: Chapter 7A ignition-resistant construction in Fire Hazard Severity Zones (WUI)
Title 24 Part 6 Energy Code + Part 11 CALGreen
High seismic (SDC D0-E) makes engineered design common
CA.note: Triennial cycle: 2022 CRC (2021 IRC base) applied 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.residentialCode: No statewide residential building code; counties and home-rule municipalities adopt their own (2015-2024 IRC in use)
CO.amendmentFlavor: Denver/Front Range mostly on amended 2021 I-codes; mountain counties amend heavily for snow load; some rural counties have no code
specialRegimes: Statewide minimum energy code (HB22-1362: 2021 IECC+ required when a jurisdiction updates codes)
Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code Board WUI rules (2025, phased into mapped WUI areas)
State plumbing and electrical codes apply statewide
CO.note: ircBase 2021 is representative of the populous Front Range; edition and snow/frost amendments vary county by county.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.residentialCode: 2022 Connecticut State Building Code — 2021 IRC portion with CT amendments, effective 2022-10-01
CT.amendmentFlavor: Statewide code that cannot be amended locally; moderate CT amendments
specialRegimes: Coastal high-wind / flood zones along Long Island Sound

DE.name: Delaware
DE.residentialCode: No statewide residential building code; the three counties and municipalities adopt their own recent IRC editions
DE.amendmentFlavor: New Castle, Kent and Sussex counties each adopt/amend the IRC on their own cycles; state role limited to fire and energy
specialRegimes: Statewide residential energy conservation code (IECC-based)
Delaware State Fire Prevention Regulations
DE.note: ircBase 2018 is representative; counties have been on 2012-2021 editions at different times.

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.residentialCode: 2017 DC Construction Codes: DC Residential Code (12B DCMR) = 2015 IRC with DC amendments, effective 2020-05-29
DC.amendmentFlavor: Heavily amended via DCMR Title 12; a 2021-I-code-based update has been in rulemaking — verify status
specialRegimes: DC Energy Conservation Code
DC Green Construction Code

FL.name: Florida
FL.residentialCode: Florida Building Code, Residential — 8th Edition (2023), 2021 IRC base, effective 2023-12-31
FL.amendmentFlavor: Standalone heavily-rewritten code: wind design integrated throughout, product approval system, sprinkler mandate removed; local amendment tightly controlled
specialRegimes: High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) provisions in Miami-Dade and Broward counties
Wind-borne debris regions with opening protection per ASCE 7 wind maps
Florida Building Code, Energy Conservation
FL.note: 9th Edition (2026) expected effective late 2026 on the triennial cycle.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.residentialCode: Georgia State Minimum Standard One- and Two-Family Dwelling Code — 2024 IRC with Georgia amendments, effective 2026-01-01
GA.amendmentFlavor: Mandatory statewide minimum administered by DCA; Georgia amendments moderate (energy and sprinkler carve-outs); locals may adopt approved local amendments
specialRegimes: Coastal counties: wind-borne debris provisions
Georgia State Minimum Standard Energy Code
GA.note: Prior base was the 2018 IRC (effective 2020-01-01); Georgia skipped the 2021 edition.

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.residentialCode: Hawaii State Building Code — state residential code based on 2018 IRC (eff. 2020-11-17), with 2021 IRC adoption recorded 2022; each county then adopts/amends its own version
HI.amendmentFlavor: State council adopts; counties must adopt within 2 years and may amend (Honolulu operates on the 2018 base); hurricane and lava-zone amendments are significant
specialRegimes: County building codes (Honolulu ROH Ch.16, Maui, Hawaii, Kauai) control in practice
Hurricane-resistant construction provisions / wind uplift
Hawaii State Energy Code
HI.note: DGS listed the 2018-based codes as current as of late 2025 even though a 2021 adoption exists; county editions lag the state code. Verify per county.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.residentialCode: Idaho Residential Code, 2020 edition (2018 IRC with Idaho amendments), effective 2021-01-01
ID.amendmentFlavor: Legislature restricts updates; energy chapters frozen/rolled back; local jurisdictions enforce
specialRegimes: High snow-load mountain jurisdictions amend ground snow values

IL.name: Illinois
IL.residentialCode: No traditional statewide residential code; Illinois Statewide Building Code (eff. 2025-01-01, Capital Development Board) sets I-code minimums for jurisdictions without their own; Chicago has its own code
IL.amendmentFlavor: Cities/counties adopt their own editions (2009-2021 common); the new CDB statewide backstop points at recent I-codes for previously code-free areas
specialRegimes: Illinois Energy Conservation Code (statewide, current IECC)
Illinois Plumbing Code (statewide, state-written)
Chicago Construction Codes (independent of the IRC)
IL.note: The exact edition designated under the 2025 statewide backstop is set by CDB rule — verify; 2021 is representative.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.residentialCode: Indiana Residential Code, 2020 edition (2018 IRC with Indiana amendments), effective 2019-12-26
IN.amendmentFlavor: Statewide, cannot be amended locally; notable deletions (sprinklers) and Indiana-specific administrative chapters
specialRegimes: Indiana energy code (amended IECC)

IA.name: Iowa
IA.residentialCode: Iowa Residential Code 2024 (2024 IRC with amendments), effective 2025-09-10
IA.amendmentFlavor: State building code adopted by the Building Code Bureau; mandatory statewide in scope but enforced only where local governments run programs
specialRegimes: State electrical (NEC 2020) and plumbing/mechanical (UPC/IMC 2021) programs
IA.note: Many rural areas have no residential inspection; larger cities (>15,000) may adopt stricter local codes.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.residentialCode: No statewide residential building code; home-rule cities/counties adopt their own (2012-2018 IRC common)
KS.amendmentFlavor: Only the Kansas Fire Prevention Code is mandatory statewide; a 2018 IRC reference exists for certain state programs
specialRegimes: Kansas Fire Prevention Code (statewide)
KS.note: ircBase 2018 is representative of Wichita/Johnson County-area jurisdictions; many rural counties have no code.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.residentialCode: 2018 Kentucky Residential Code, 3rd edition (based on 2015 IRC), effective 2024-08-01
KY.amendmentFlavor: Kentucky publishes its own editions on a 2015 IRC base with successive KY amendment editions; statewide, administered by DHBC
specialRegimes: 2023 NEC adopted statewide effective 2025-01-01
KY.note: The 'edition year' in Kentucky code titles (2018 KRC) is the KY publication year, not the IRC base year.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.residentialCode: 2021 Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code — Residential (2021 IRC base), effective 2023-01-01
LA.amendmentFlavor: LSUCC adopted statewide post-Katrina; wind design amendments significant; parishes enforce
specialRegimes: Hurricane wind design per ASCE 7; coastal parishes in wind-borne debris regions
Flood-resistant construction (ASCE 24 / FEMA) in coastal zones

ME.name: Maine
ME.residentialCode: MUBEC (Maine Uniform Building and Energy Code) Residential — 2021 IRC base, effective 2025-04-07
ME.amendmentFlavor: Statewide code; enforcement mandatory only in municipalities over 4,000 population — smaller towns may not inspect
specialRegimes: MUBEC energy chapters (IECC-based)
Heavy ground snow loads (50-100+ psf) set locally

MD.name: Maryland
MD.residentialCode: Maryland Building Performance Standards (MBPS) Residential — 2021 IRC base, effective 2023-05-29; local jurisdictions implement and may amend
MD.amendmentFlavor: State sets a uniform edition statewide; counties (Montgomery, Baltimore, etc.) layer significant local amendments
specialRegimes: Maryland state sprinkler mandate for new one- and two-family dwellings
MBPS energy standards (IECC-based)
MD.note: Maryland boards began adopting 2024 editions in late 2025 (e.g., Board of Plumbing residential code, eff. 2025-11-24); the MBPS-wide 2024 update may already be in force — verify.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.residentialCode: Massachusetts State Building Code 780 CMR, 10th edition, Residential Volume (2021 IRC base), effective 2024-10-11
MA.amendmentFlavor: Heavily amended (MA-specific structural, means-of-egress and administrative provisions); uniform statewide, no local structural amendments
specialRegimes: Stretch Energy Code and opt-in Specialized code (DOER) adopted by most municipalities
Coastal wind zones (110+ mph Vult) on Cape Cod and islands

MI.name: Michigan
MI.residentialCode: 2021 Michigan Residential Code (2021 IRC base), effective 2025-08-29
MI.amendmentFlavor: Statewide code under the Stille-DeRossett-Hale act; LARA rules amend the IRC moderately; local units enforce but cannot amend technical provisions
specialRegimes: Michigan Uniform Energy Code
MI.note: Replaced the long-running 2015 Michigan Residential Code (eff. 2016-02-08).

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.residentialCode: 2020 Minnesota Residential Code (2018 IRC base), effective 2020-03-31
MN.amendmentFlavor: State code is the sole standard where enforced, but municipal enforcement of the residential chapters is optional outside the Twin Cities metro
specialRegimes: Minnesota residential energy code (state-written amendments)
60-in typical frost depths in the north; heavy ground snow loads
MN.note: Minnesota adopts every other IRC edition; the next code (2024 IRC base) was in rulemaking as of 2025-2026 — verify.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.residentialCode: Local option: jurisdictions that regulate must use a designated recent IRC edition (Mississippi Residential Code 2024 = 2024 IRC, designated eff. 2025-01-01); counties may opt out
MS.amendmentFlavor: State Building Codes Council designates editions; adoption/enforcement is a local choice and many rural counties opted out
specialRegimes: Six southern coastal counties: mandatory wind/hurricane code enforcement post-Katrina
MS.note: ircBase 2024 reflects the current state designation; jurisdictions may lawfully be on any of the three latest editions.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.residentialCode: No statewide residential building code; cities/counties adopt their own (2015-2021 IRC common; St. Louis County and Kansas City maintain amended codes)
MO.amendmentFlavor: Local editions and amendments vary widely; only state modular-housing program references the IRC (2021 IRC eff. 2024-11-30)
specialRegimes: State modular residential program (2021 IRC base)
MO.note: ircBase 2018 is representative of metro jurisdictions; many rural counties have no residential code.

MT.name: Montana
MT.residentialCode: Montana Residential Code — 2021 IRC with Montana amendments (residential adoption eff. 2022-06-11; full 2021 suite updated 2024-09-21)
MT.amendmentFlavor: State code administered by DLI; 1-2 family permits/inspections happen only in certified local government jurisdictions
specialRegimes: High ground snow loads by county (state snow load study)
2021 IWUIC available for local WUI adoption
MT.note: Outside certified jurisdictions there is no residential building permit program (electrical/plumbing state permits still apply).

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.residentialCode: Nebraska Residential Code = 2018 IRC (state building code, eff. 2019-04-17); locals may adopt/amend if generally conforming
NE.amendmentFlavor: Statute adopts the IRC with few amendments; cities like Omaha/Lincoln amend locally; enforcement is local
specialRegimes: NEC 2023 statewide effective 2024-08-01

NV.name: Nevada
NV.residentialCode: No statewide residential code for private construction; counties/cities adopt their own (Clark County/Las Vegas on recent ICC suites; State Public Works adopted 2024 IRC for state buildings eff. 2024-11-15)
NV.amendmentFlavor: Clark and Washoe counties run large amended code programs; rural counties vary
specialRegimes: Statewide energy code (IECC-based) mandated by statute
Seismic D in western Nevada; Tahoe-area snow loads
NV.note: ircBase 2021 is representative; southern Nevada jurisdictions were transitioning to the 2024 suite in 2025-2026.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.residentialCode: NH State Building Code — Residential = 2024 IRC with NH amendments, effective 2026-07-01
NH.amendmentFlavor: Biennial legislative updates (2021 base ran 2024-07-01 to 2026-06-30); municipalities may adopt more-stringent local amendments with state approval; enforcement local
specialRegimes: NH energy code amendments (reduced from model IECC)

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.residentialCode: NJ Uniform Construction Code — One- & Two-Family Dwelling Subcode = 2021 IRC/NJ edition, effective 2022-09-06
NJ.amendmentFlavor: UCC is uniform statewide with no local amendments; NJ edition modifies the IRC substantially (administrative + technical)
specialRegimes: Coastal A/V flood zones (post-Sandy elevation standards)
NJ energy subcode (IECC-based)
NJ.note: UpCodes shows the 2021 subcode scheduled to be superseded 2026-08-16, implying a 2024-base update — verify.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.residentialCode: 2021 New Mexico Residential Building Code (2021 IRC base), effective 2023-12-14
NM.amendmentFlavor: CID-administered statewide code; includes NM Earthen Building Materials Code for adobe construction
specialRegimes: New Mexico Earthen Building Materials Code (adobe/rammed earth)
NM residential energy conservation code

NY.name: New York
NY.residentialCode: 2025 Residential Code of New York State (2024 IRC base), effective 2025-12-31
NY.amendmentFlavor: Uniform Code applies statewide outside NYC; moderate NYS amendments; local governments may adopt more-restrictive standards with state approval
specialRegimes: New York City Construction Codes (entirely separate from the NYS Uniform Code)
NYS Energy Conservation Construction Code
NY.note: The 2020 RCNYS (2018 IRC base) governed 2020-05-12 through 2025-12-30; transition provisions may allow either code briefly.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.residentialCode: 2018 North Carolina Residential Code (2015 IRC base), effective 2019-01-01 — still in force
NC.amendmentFlavor: NC rewrites the IRC significantly (own bracing and appendix provisions); legislature repeatedly postponed the 2024 NCRC (2021 IRC base) and restricted residential re-adoption
specialRegimes: Coastal wind zones and wind-borne debris regions (Outer Banks)
NC-specific wall-bracing and deck amendments
NC.note: 2024 NCRC (2021 IRC base) shown as pending/postponed as of 2026-08-13 (S.L. 2024-57, S.L. 2025-2 delays) — verify before assuming the new edition.

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.residentialCode: North Dakota Residential Code 2024 (2024 IRC base), effective 2026-01-01 (ND State Building Code)
ND.amendmentFlavor: State publishes the code with ND amendments; jurisdictions that enforce a building code must use it (may add local modifications); many rural areas do not enforce
specialRegimes: Deep frost depths (~48+ in) and high snow loads
ND.note: Prior edition: 2021 IRC base, effective 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.residentialCode: 2019 Residential Code of Ohio for One-, Two- and Three-Family Dwellings (2018 IRC base), effective 2019-07-01
OH.amendmentFlavor: Statewide RCO (OAC 4101:8) with Ohio amendments; note it covers three-family dwellings too; local building departments enforce
specialRegimes: Ohio residential energy provisions (amended IECC)
OH.note: An RCO update (2021/2024 base) was under committee review — verify current rule status at codes.ohio.gov.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.residentialCode: Oklahoma Residential Code = 2018 IRC with OK amendments (OUBCC statewide minimum), effective 2022-09-14
OK.amendmentFlavor: OUBCC sets the minimum; municipalities may amend (commonly up); unincorporated/rural enforcement is thin
specialRegimes: Tornado-prone: storm shelter appendix and wind provisions frequently amended locally

OR.name: Oregon
OR.residentialCode: 2023 Oregon Residential Specialty Code (2021 IRC base), effective 2023-10-01 (mandatory 2024-04-01)
OR.amendmentFlavor: BCD rewrites the IRC into the ORSC; uniform statewide, no local technical amendments
specialRegimes: ICC 600-2020 standard for coastal high-wind regions
Oregon Residential Reach Code (optional energy path)
Seismic D in western Oregon

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.residentialCode: PA Uniform Construction Code — Pennsylvania Residential Code = 2021 IRC with PA amendments, effective 2026-01-01
PA.amendmentFlavor: UCC statewide; ~90% of municipalities administer it locally (opt-in), others use state enforcement; RAC filters which model-code changes are adopted
specialRegimes: PA alternative residential energy provisions

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.residentialCode: Rhode Island Residential Code SBC-2 (2021 IRC base), effective 2025-12-01
RI.amendmentFlavor: Statewide, no local amendments; note the prior 'SBC-2-2021' edition (eff. 2022-02-01) was actually based on the 2018 IRC
specialRegimes: Coastal wind/flood provisions (hurricane exposure)

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.residentialCode: South Carolina Residential Code (2021 IRC with SC amendments), effective 2023-01-01
SC.amendmentFlavor: Building Codes Council adopts statewide with SC modifications (notably to energy chapters); local enforcement mandatory
specialRegimes: Charleston-area seismic (SDC D) — engineered lateral design common
Coastal wind-borne debris region
SC.note: SC reviews each new edition on a ~3-year cycle; a 2024-base update may follow — verify.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.residentialCode: No statewide residential code; municipalities that adopt construction standards must use state-designated editions (statute references the 2021 IBC); IRC adoption is local (Sioux Falls, Rapid City on recent editions)
SD.amendmentFlavor: State designates editions but does not mandate residential enforcement; rural areas largely uninspected
specialRegimes: NEC statewide (2023 NEC eff. 2024-11-12)
SD.note: ircBase 2021 is representative of the larger cities.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.residentialCode: Tennessee statewide residential code = 2018 IRC with TN amendments (State Fire Marshal's Office), effective 2020-07-16
TN.amendmentFlavor: SFMO program covers jurisdictions without their own; local govts may adopt one of the three most recent editions or opt out by two-thirds vote (some counties are exempt)
specialRegimes: Reduced statewide energy requirements (2009-2018 IECC mix for dwellings)
TN.note: Opt-out counties have no residential inspections; cities like Nashville run their own newer codes.

TX.name: Texas
TX.residentialCode: No statewide adoption/enforcement; by statute (Loc. Gov't Code §214.212) the IRC 'as it existed on May 1, 2012' is the municipal residential code, and cities routinely adopt current editions with local amendments; unincorporated areas largely unregulated
TX.amendmentFlavor: Big-city editions range 2015-2024 with heavy local amendment packages (Houston, Dallas, Austin, San Antonio all differ); counties generally cannot enforce building codes
specialRegimes: TDI/TWIA windstorm certification along the Gulf coast (2024 IRC-based standard eff. 2026-04-01)
Industrialized (modular) housing program: 2021 IRC eff. 2024-07-01
Municipal amendments must be reviewed for insurance-rated windstorm compliance in seaward counties
TX.note: ircBase 2021 is representative of major metros; the statutory 2012 baseline only sets the floor for municipalities.

UT.name: Utah
UT.residentialCode: Utah Residential Code (2021 IRC with substantial legislative amendments, Utah Code Title 15A), effective 2023-07-01
UT.amendmentFlavor: Legislature adopts and amends directly in statute: sprinkler mandate removed, energy chapters modified, Utah snow-load study replaces map values
specialRegimes: Utah-specific ground snow load study (by elevation)
Wasatch Front seismic (SDC D)

VT.name: Vermont
VT.residentialCode: No statewide residential building code for detached one- and two-family homes; Residential Building Energy Standards (RBES) apply statewide; Fire & Building Safety Code covers public buildings and multifamily
VT.amendmentFlavor: Towns may adopt local codes (e.g., Burlington); single-family construction is otherwise governed only by RBES energy certification
specialRegimes: RBES / CBES energy standards (statewide, self-certified)
Vermont Fire and Building Safety Code (2015 base) for non-exempt buildings

VA.name: Virginia
VA.residentialCode: Virginia USBC — Virginia Residential Code 2021 (2021 IRC base), effective 2024-01-18
VA.amendmentFlavor: Uniform statewide; no local technical amendments allowed; VA amendments moderate; triennial cycle (2024-base update expected ~2027)
specialRegimes: Coastal wind zones (Hampton Roads / Eastern Shore)

WA.name: Washington
WA.residentialCode: 2021 Washington State Residential Code (2021 IRC with WA amendments), effective 2024-03-15
WA.amendmentFlavor: SBCC amends heavily (especially energy/ventilation); statewide uniform; locals may amend residential only within limits
specialRegimes: Washington State Energy Code — Residential (state-written, among the strictest in the US)
Seismic D/D2 west of the Cascades
WUI code provisions in mapped areas
WA.note: 2024-base cycle already scheduled: adoption August-September 2026, effective 2027-05-03.

WV.name: West Virginia
WV.residentialCode: West Virginia Residential Code = 2018 IRC (State Building Code, 87 CSR 4), effective 2022-08-01 — applies only in jurisdictions that opt in
WV.amendmentFlavor: State Fire Commission promulgates the code content; counties/municipalities choose whether to adopt and enforce it; many do not
specialRegimes: State Fire Code (87 CSR 1) statewide

WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.residentialCode: Wisconsin Uniform Dwelling Code (SPS 320-325) — state-written code for one- and two-family dwellings, statewide since 1980 (last major update eff. 2022-06-01)
WI.amendmentFlavor: NOT an IRC adoption: Wisconsin's own prescriptive tables (studs, joists, rafters, bracing) differ from IRC numbering and some values; municipalities enforce, no local technical amendments
specialRegimes: UDC energy chapter (SPS 322, roughly 2009-IECC-era stringency)
Commercial/multifamily use IBC-based SPS 361-366
WI.note: Inference engines must not assume IRC section numbers or IRC bracing methods in Wisconsin.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.residentialCode: No statewide residential building code; cities/counties adopt their own (Cheyenne, Casper on recent IRC editions)
WY.amendmentFlavor: State Fire Marshal adopts codes for state buildings only; local editions range roughly 2015-2024
specialRegimes: High snow loads and frost depths in mountain jurisdictions
WY.note: ircBase 2018 is representative; many rural counties have no residential code.

CA-ON-S.name: Canada · Ontario — South (GTA / Golden Horseshoe)
CA-ON-S.residentialCode: 2024 Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 163/24), adopting NBC 2020 plus the Ontario Amendments — effective 2025-01-01
CA-ON-S.amendmentFlavor: Ontario adopts NBC 2020 by reference plus a published amendment document; the 2024 harmonization removed roughly 1,730 technical variations from the national codes. Part 9 wood framing is largely unamended.
specialRegimes: NBC Division B Part 9 — Housing and Small Buildings (buildings up to 3 storeys and 600 m2)
MMAH Supplementary Standard SB-1 (climatic and seismic data by municipality) — governs snow load and frost depth, not NBC Appendix C
MMAH Supplementary Standard SB-7 (joist, rafter, beam and lintel span tables, by species group)
CA-ON-S.note: NOT an IRC adoption. Framing rules come from NBC Division B Part 9 (9.23 Wood-Frame Construction); inference engines must not assume IRC section numbers or IRC braced-wall-panel methods here. NBC 9.23.13 selects lateral bracing from Sa(0.2) and hourly wind pressure rather than braced-wall lines.

CA-ON-E.name: Canada · Ontario — East (Ottawa Valley / Kingston)
CA-ON-E.residentialCode: 2024 Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 163/24), adopting NBC 2020 plus the Ontario Amendments — effective 2025-01-01
CA-ON-E.amendmentFlavor: Same code as the rest of Ontario; this entry differs only in climatic and seismic data (SB-1) for the Ottawa Valley.
specialRegimes: NBC Division B Part 9 — Housing and Small Buildings (buildings up to 3 storeys and 600 m2)
MMAH Supplementary Standard SB-1 (climatic and seismic data by municipality)
MMAH Supplementary Standard SB-7 (span tables)
CA-ON-E.note: NOT an IRC adoption. Framing rules come from NBC Division B Part 9 (9.23 Wood-Frame Construction); inference engines must not assume IRC section numbers or IRC braced-wall-panel methods here. NBC 9.23.13 selects lateral bracing from Sa(0.2) and hourly wind pressure rather than braced-wall lines.

CA-ON-N.name: Canada · Ontario — North (Sudbury / Thunder Bay)
CA-ON-N.residentialCode: 2024 Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 163/24), adopting NBC 2020 plus the Ontario Amendments — effective 2025-01-01
CA-ON-N.amendmentFlavor: Same code as the rest of Ontario; this entry differs only in climatic data (SB-1) for northern Ontario.
specialRegimes: NBC Division B Part 9 — Housing and Small Buildings (buildings up to 3 storeys and 600 m2)
MMAH Supplementary Standard SB-1 (climatic and seismic data by municipality)
MMAH Supplementary Standard SB-7 (span tables)
CA-ON-N.note: NOT an IRC adoption. Framing rules come from NBC Division B Part 9 (9.23 Wood-Frame Construction); inference engines must not assume IRC section numbers or IRC braced-wall-panel methods here. NBC 9.23.13 selects lateral bracing from Sa(0.2) and hourly wind pressure rather than braced-wall lines.

CA-BC.name: Canada · British Columbia
CA-BC.residentialCode: BC Building Code 2024 (NBC 2020 base), in force 2024
CA-BC.amendmentFlavor: BC publishes its own code book on the NBC base, with substantial provincial amendments. Vancouver enforces its own separate Vancouver Building By-law.
specialRegimes: NBC Division B Part 9 — Housing and Small Buildings (buildings up to 3 storeys and 600 m2)
BC Energy Step Code — mandatory performance tiers that commonly drive thicker or double-stud exterior walls
High seismic: coastal BC exceeds the NBC 9.23.13 prescriptive bracing threshold, requiring Part 4 engineered lateral design
CA-BC.note: NOT an IRC adoption. Framing rules come from NBC Division B Part 9 (9.23 Wood-Frame Construction); inference engines must not assume IRC section numbers or IRC braced-wall-panel methods here. NBC 9.23.13 selects lateral bracing from Sa(0.2) and hourly wind pressure rather than braced-wall lines.

CA-AB.name: Canada · Alberta
CA-AB.residentialCode: Alberta Building Code 2023 (NBC 2020 base), in force 2023
CA-AB.amendmentFlavor: Alberta publishes its own code book on the NBC base with modest provincial amendments; Part 9 framing is close to the national text.
specialRegimes: NBC Division B Part 9 — Housing and Small Buildings (buildings up to 3 storeys and 600 m2)
CA-AB.note: NOT an IRC adoption. Framing rules come from NBC Division B Part 9 (9.23 Wood-Frame Construction); inference engines must not assume IRC section numbers or IRC braced-wall-panel methods here. NBC 9.23.13 selects lateral bracing from Sa(0.2) and hourly wind pressure rather than braced-wall lines.

CA-SK.name: Canada · Saskatchewan
CA-SK.residentialCode: National Building Code of Canada 2020 (Division B Part 9), adopted 2024-01-01
CA-SK.amendmentFlavor: Direct adoption under The Construction Codes Act; Saskatchewan skipped NBC 2015 entirely, moving from NBC 2010 to NBC 2020. Among the closest jurisdictions to the unmodified national code.
specialRegimes: NBC Division B Part 9 — Housing and Small Buildings (buildings up to 3 storeys and 600 m2)
CA-SK.note: NOT an IRC adoption. Framing rules come from NBC Division B Part 9 (9.23 Wood-Frame Construction); inference engines must not assume IRC section numbers or IRC braced-wall-panel methods here. NBC 9.23.13 selects lateral bracing from Sa(0.2) and hourly wind pressure rather than braced-wall lines.

CA-MB.name: Canada · Manitoba
CA-MB.residentialCode: Manitoba Building Code (M.R. 78/2023), adopting NBC 2020 — effective 2024-01-01
CA-MB.amendmentFlavor: NBC 2020 with Manitoba amendments, which the province has been actively reducing under its Canadian Free Trade Agreement commitments. Manitoba also skipped NBC 2015.
specialRegimes: NBC Division B Part 9 — Housing and Small Buildings (buildings up to 3 storeys and 600 m2)
CA-MB.note: NOT an IRC adoption.
